citation.title: Dietary Macronutrients Do Not Differently Influence Postprandial Serum and Plasma Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Concentrations: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Controlled Cross-Over Trial

reported.what: serum BDNF, pg/mL, mean +/- SD (n = 18) after the high-fat meal at T0, T60 and T240 min (the high-carbohydrate and high-protein rows of the same table are the same kind of value)
EDTA plasma BDNF, pg/mL, mean +/- SD (n = 18) after the same three meals at T0, T60 and T240 min
plasma glucose, mmol/L, median with 25th to 75th percentiles, fasting and after each meal (the glucose and insulin curves of the abstract are in Supplementary Figure 2 only)

detail: The meal-test glucose and insulin (Table 5, 0 to 240 min after three high-fat meals) are medians with 25th to 75th percentiles, which the model's statistics cannot hold; the curves themselves are only in a supplementary figure outside the XML. The paper's main outcome, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, has no model state either (marker/bdnf).
